<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (32 routes)`, `environmentId (46 routes)`, `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 51 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **195** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e93250d1a7258b33f8d0dfed8ffac2733eb6aed6` — the merge of head `83b7676fe9211f81bce069e3ba5df0642ef41ffb` into base `e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e93250d1a7258b33f8d0dfed8ffac2733eb6aed6 && git checkout e93250d1a7258b33f8d0dfed8ffac2733eb6aed6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed 83b7676fe9211f81bce069e3ba5df0642ef41ffb && git checkout -B drift-repro e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed && git merge --no-ff 83b7676fe9211f81bce069e3ba5df0642ef41ffb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e4f5e56c017ca2b2b028c7700b88c5ae9e677eed` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Contract-tier review (L2) — PASS with should-fix · head `16e4a54c277b3083ed97259340fd2f36af621795`.** Reviewed by an isolated `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` thread, read-only. The PR merges cleanly into `origin/main`, and all 69 check-runs are success or skipped.

**What holds**
- **One judgment.** The verdict, its exemptions and its refusal live only in the core module. The dispatcher hunk is a pure extraction.
- **Every REST data door.** Each one reaches the judgment through the single identity resolution.
- **Skip conditions.** They are identical, and both plugins read the same values.
- **No steering.** No client value moves the environment the judgment reads.

**Should-fix — close these, then a delta read**
1. Changeset: a `(narrowing)` change carries the **BREAKING** banner and `!` in the title, as every other narrowing changeset on the tree does.
2. PR body, report comment and changeset (~:20): state the positive rule only, *every data door judges environment membership*. Drop the sentences that name host shapes or describe what a construction leaves unjudged.
3. `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (~1089): the key's describe text names every door the switch governs, not one.
4. `rest-environment-membership-door.test.ts`: pin both precedence claims the body makes. Today, removing either guard term at `rest-server.ts` ~3622/~3624 turns no test red. Also add a `/meta` row.

**Nits**
- At `rest-server.ts` ~3624, say why gate-held sessions are not judged there.
- Carry the moved caching caution into the core docblock.

**Open questions:** the defaults of direct constructions stay with the security seat. They are not reachable in this repository.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `83b7676fe9211f81bce069e3ba5df0642ef41ffb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/sec2-r7gg.md, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/core/src/security/environment-membership.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-environment-membership-door.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + none

### ① Derived judgments

Every REST data door judges environment membership through one judgment in `@objectstack/core`. The dispatcher hunk is a pure extraction into that module. The skip conditions are identical on both doors, and both plugins read the same switch value. No client value moves the environment the judgment reads: the organization comes from the vetted session or key, never from a header.

Review trail:
- Full review: comment 7073478084 (PASS with four should-fix items).
- Isolated delta re-review at `09c96f433`: PASS. Items 1, 3 and 4 were closed; two wording should-fixes remained open.
- This head is `09c96f433` plus one commit, `83b7676fe`, which touches only comments. It rewords the `rest-server.ts` constructor doc to state the positive rule, and the test-fixture docblock. The seat read it under the review downgrade; it changes no code line. The report comment's summary was edited to state the rule and the counts only.
- CI at this head: 58 success, 11 expected skips, 0 failed. `landing-k` OK, K = 6.

### ② Semver level

`patch`, as declared: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset and the title carry the BREAKING banner and `!`.

### ③ Boundary flags

The change narrows the accept-set: a caller who is not a member of the environment is now refused at every data door. No key, value or default of the metadata protocol changes. SQL push-down: none added.

### ④ Design judgment

One judgment with one resolution path, so no door can drift from the others. Both should-fix items from the delta re-review are closed at this head. No must-fix or should-fix is open; only nits remain. The defaults of direct constructions are held by the security seat as an open question; they are not reachable in this repository.
